title: Isolate legacy token validators into sandbox; upgrade JWT/SAML stacks and staged rollout
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: Our token validation stack includes legacy adapters that call into older OpenSSL/JWT/SAML libraries. Multiple transitive CVEs and subtle parsing differences have been identified in dependent libraries, and we need a path to safely upgrade without breaking older clients. Goal: isolate legacy validators into a sandboxed compatibility adapter, upgrade primary validation path to modern libs (OpenSSL 3.x compatible build, jose 2.x, saml2 library rewrite), and roll the changes out via feature flags and canary routing. Deliverables: sandbox adapter, new adapter + tests, integration test matrix, perf benchmarks, staged rollout plan with automatic rollback triggers.
acceptance_criteria: New validator implementation passes unit + integration tests across 3 canonical token shapes (JWT compact, JWS detached, SAML assertion)
No functional regressions for existing clients verified via e2e smoke on opt-in canary (5% of traffic) for 48h
Latency increase on auth path < 5th percentile +5ms compared to baseline; P95 increase < 10ms
Security review signed off and SBOM updated for all services touched
Migration & rollback playbooks documented and rehearsed with oncall
migration_plan: 1) Introduce adapter interface (AuthService.Validator) and move legacy code behind CompatibilityValidator feature-flag. 2) Implement NewValidator using jose 2.x and saml2-rewrite; run full unit test suite. 3) Deploy to staging, run token-parade test harness (confluence link) to validate behavioral parity. 4) Canary to 5% traffic in production behind feature flag for 48h with automated anomaly detection on 5 metrics (errors, latencies, auth-failures, CPU, memory). 5) Gradually increase to 25% then 100% if no regressions. 6) Decommission sandboxed legacy validator after 30 days of stability and remove feature flag.
rollback_plan: Immediate rollback to previous stable image if any of the following are detected during canary: auth error rate spike > 0.1%, unexplained token decoding failures, P95 latency > baseline +20ms, or memory leak > 100MB over 1h. Rollback steps: toggle feature flag off, route traffic to pre-upgrade version, create incident and tag owners. Postmortem within 72h.
